paper_metadata.title: Effect of Chromium on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Nb–Si Hypoeutectic and Eutectic Alloys

evidence.quote: Our present investigation is to study the effect of chromium on the microstructure of Nb–Si hypoeutectic and eutectic alloys.

For the Nb 81.3Si10Cr8.7 alloy, the suction cast microstructure is shown in Fig. 2d, revealing the presence of primary (Nb) ss dendrites and flaky Nb 3Si, Cr2Nb (black) along with finer scale eutectic (Nb) ss/Nb3Si and (Nb) ss/Cr2Nb.

The suction cast sample (Fig. 4a) of Nb 90Si10 alloy reveals the presence of primary (Nb) ss dendrites with a relatively large amount of eutectic between (Nb) ss and Nb3Si.

Dendritic (Nb)ss, blocky Cr 2Nb and rod shaped Nb 3Si phases along with two eutectic ((Nb) ss ? Nb3Si) and ((Nb) ss ? Cr2Nb) are observed in the microstructure of Nb 80Si5Cr15 alloy.

These in situ composites of pre-set compositions were synthesized by suction casting vacuum-arc-melting-cum casting technique under high purity argon atmosphere. The as-cast alloys were prepared using the high purity (99.9%) elements. To ensure compositional and chemical homogeneity, the as-cast buttons were re-melted 4–5 times.
Subsequently, the as-cast cylinders were synthesized by novel arc melting cum suction casting using the water cooled split copper mould to obtain cylindrical rods of diameter ( u) = 5 mm.
The cooling rate of the suction cast mould in this technique varies from 10 2 to 10 3 K/min
It reveals the presence of (Nb) ss dendrites and large rod like Nb 3Si,Cr2-Nb (black) along with eutectic (Nb) ss/Nb3Si and (Nb) ss/Cr2Nb
The eutectic between ((Nb) ss ? Nb3Si) exhibits rod-shaped eutectic whereas ((Nb) ss ? b-Nb5Si3) shows lamellar eutectic.

The mechanical properties of these Nb–Si–Cr alloys depend on the volume fraction of ductile dendritic (Nb) ss, hard and brittle silicide and Laves phase, eutectic phase, interlamellar spacing and solid solution strengthening.

During solidification, the Nb 3Si formation is suppressed and b-Nb5Si3 liquidus is extended below the peritectic isotherm and intersects with the (Nb) ss liquidus to form a metastable eutectic reaction.
The peaks of the diffraction patterns of the binary alloys are indexed as primary (Nb) ss (Im3m, a = 0.3306 nm)
while rest are Nb 3Si (P42/n, a = 1.021 nm and c = 0.517 nm)

For Nb 81.3-Si18.7 and Nb 81.3Si8.7Cr10 alloys, the volume fraction of ductile dendritic (Nb) ss phases are (17.8 ± 0.3) % and (67 ± 3.2) % respectively.

The mechanical properties of these Nb–Si–Cr alloys depend on the volume fraction of ductile dendritic (Nb) ss, hard and brittle silicide and Laves phase, eutectic phase, interlamellar spacing and solid solution strengthening.

The strength and plasticity of these alloys cannot directly be correlated with any single factor. The mechanical properties of these Nb–Si–Cr alloys depend on the volume fraction of ductile dendritic (Nb) ss, hard and brittle silicide and Laves phase, eutectic phase, interlamellar spacing and solid solution strengthening.

from the above discussion it is clear that plasticity variation for both eutectic and hypoeutectic alloys are mainly controlled by the volume fraction of the ductile (Nb) ss whereas strength is controlled by the volume fraction of eutectic phases.
